title: The Light That Shouldn't Be
status: story round v2, approved on 5 Nov 2026 with the 19 decisions of its approval sheet and the two scope decisions of that evening. Built from the approved story skeleton v1, then changed after the review of the same day. Three review changes wait for approval: every kit has a home islet, the third light is a home signal station, and the solo timing (docs/story/README.md, section 'Changes to the approval sheet after the review').
about: The whole case for one crew: cards, routes, deductions, the Night of Three Lights, the accusation, the reveal, rewards and the Relighting. The format is described field by field in backend/content/README.md, section 'The case data'. The story reasons are in docs/story/CASE-FILE.md.

where_it_lives.why: D016: server only and never served. The file names the culprit, and the game build must never pick it up.

spoiler_warning: This repository is public, so anyone can read this file. It names the culprit. In the game, the culprit reaches only crews that solved the case.
premise: Lighthouses on the Saltreach Isles keep losing their lenses. On some nights a light flashes the harbor alarm, long, short, long, from the open sea where no lighthouse stands. Ships that answer it are wrecked on the Teeth. The harbor master has posted a reward for whoever finds the light.
question: Who is the 'someone out at sea' in Elena's log, and where does the light hide?

suspects.title: the fisherman in the yellow coat
suspects.on_the_surface: The man with the red boat. Elena's log says not to trust him, and she told you he uses her light to guide the smugglers in. In the rescue ending the coastguard took him, yet he is free again.
suspects.refused_line: Refused. D2: the crates carry the Harbor Office seal, and the fisherman only carries them for pay. He is a smuggler, not the captain.

suspects.title: the salvage foreman
suspects.on_the_surface: Runs Greyfathom's yard at Wreck Point and buys whatever the wrecks leave behind. Every wreck is good business for the yard.
suspects.refused_line: Refused. D3: the lenses are held for an owner whose post goes to the Harbor Office. The foreman only runs the yard.

suspects.title: the coastguard commander
suspects.on_the_surface: Commands the cutter at the harbor's signal station. On the wreck nights, nobody answered the alarm.
suspects.refused_line: Refused. D4: on every wreck night, Harbor Office orders sent the cutter away. The commander obeyed and wrote it down.

suspects.title: the harbor master
suspects.on_the_surface: Runs the Harbor Office. Nobody has met him face to face, only his lit window across the bay. He posted the reward, and Elena's log says to tell him.

log_card.source: story.json desk note shown after read_log (Story v2, change 6). Story v2 owns that text.
log_card.board_lead: From Elena's log: a page was torn out right after 'Tell the harbor master.' Two words still show through: 'old watchtower'.
log_card.what_it_saves: C8's lead is on the crew board from the start. After D3, a log reader finds the torn page at once (route C8.log_reader, no 5 minute search).

continuity_lines.text: The harbor jail's only cell is empty. A release order is pinned to the door: 'Release the fisherman. By order of the Harbor Office.' It is stamped with a small seal: an anchor with an open eye.
continuity_lines.shown_to: every player who has not solved the case. Solvers see the jailed harbor master instead (relighting.spoiler_rule).

cards.title: The reward notice
cards.lead: The harbor master has posted a notice about a strange light.
cards.text: REWARD. On some nights a light flashes the harbor alarm, long, short, long, from the open sea west of the Teeth. No lighthouse stands there, and none ever has. Ships that answer it are lost on the reef. Whoever finds the light will be paid from the harbor purse. Report to the Harbor Office. By order of the harbor master.

routes.found_line: The notice is nailed to the board outside the Harbor Office. The ink is still fresh.

cards.title: Fog nights only
cards.lead: Someone knows which nights the ships were lost.
cards.text: All three wrecks this season happened on nights of thick fog. They are the three nights Elena circled in her tide tables. On clear nights, nobody has seen the light.

routes.found_line: You remember the locked tower door. On the stairs below, the fisherman talked into a radio: 'No fog tonight. We wait for the next one.'
The ferry is in, so the clerk has time for you. The sailing log shows crossings cancelled for fog on all three wreck nights.
The ferry clerk copies the sailing log for 150 coins. Crossings were cancelled for fog on all three wreck nights.

cards.title: The seal on your key
cards.lead: Look closely at the key you carry.
cards.text: The tag on your brass key reads TOWER DOOR. It is stamped with a small seal: an anchor with an open eye. Held to the lantern, tiny letters show under the seal: CUT AND SEALED BY THE HARBOR OFFICE.

routes.found_line: You hold the tag to your lantern and turn it until the light catches the brass.

cards.title: Sealed crates
cards.lead: The smugglers at the cove are moving crates.
cards.text: Crates from the wrecks. Every lid is stamped with a seal: an anchor with an open eye. Chalked on each lid is the smugglers' rule: 'Carry only. Never open. Paid per crate.'

routes.found_line: You show the fisherman's red token. The doorman sends a boy for the tally man, and you wait by the fire until he lets you into the back room.
At low tide you wade into the cave under the cove, your lantern held high. The crates are stacked above the waterline.
The doorman counts your 200 coins twice, then makes you wait until the back room is empty. You get one look.
A sealed crate has washed up on your beach after the fog. The chalk on its lid is still readable.

cards.title: Greyfathom's manifest
cards.lead: Greyfathom's yard keeps a record of what the wrecks bring in.
cards.closed_line: The yard is busy with crates. You do not know what to ask about yet.
cards.text: MANIFEST, Greyfathom Salvage, Wreck Point. Taken from the wrecks on the Teeth this season: 12 lighthouse lenses, crated and sealed. Not for sale. Hold for the owner. At the bottom, in chalk: a small drawing of a tower.

routes.found_line: Nobody on this coast knows your face, so the foreman hires you for a shift and asks no questions. When it ends, the manifest lies open in the yard office.
You start waiting at the change of shift and sit out the whole shift by the gate. When it ends, the foreman pins the new manifest to it.
A dockhand on the beach takes 250 coins and makes you wait while he copies the manifest by hand.

cards.title: The owner's post
cards.closed_line: The Harbor Office is busy. You do not know what to look for yet.
cards.text: The Harbor Office keeps a pigeonhole stamped with the seal, an anchor with an open eye. It is labelled GREYFATHOM SALVAGE, OWNER. In it lies a payment slip for every wreck this season, each marked with a small chalk tower.

routes.found_line: Your keeper's permit opens the post room behind the Harbor Office. Your own pigeonhole is empty. The one next to it is not.
The mail boat is in. You watch the clerk sort the post: one bundle goes to the back, into a pigeonhole stamped with the seal.
The day clerk pockets 200 coins and lets you look through the post rack while he counts them.
As a Greyfathom shareholder you may read the register. The owner's post goes to the Harbor Office, with a payment for every wreck.

cards.title: The coastguard night log
cards.lead: The coastguard writes down every alarm.
cards.text: The coastguard's night log. On each of the three wreck nights, the same entry: 'Alarm seen at sea. Cutter ordered to the far side of the isles by the Harbor Office. Unable to answer.'

routes.found_line: The coastguard commander opens the night log for you at the signal station. 'We answer every alarm we are allowed to.'

cards.title: The torn page
cards.lead: Something is hidden in the old watchtower on the Teeth.
cards.closed_line: Rain blows through the old watchtower. The walls are full of loose stones, and you do not know which one to try yet.
cards.text: A page torn from Elena's logbook, the one after 'Tell the harbor master.' In her shaking hand: 'I was wrong to trust the office. He never comes ashore after dark. His window is a lie: his night clerk keeps the lamp burning. The lenses go to the old watchtower.' Across the top, in another hand: 'Found in her desk. Left at the drop, as you asked.'

routes.found_line: Your brass key opens the rusted door of the old tower. Inside, one stone is marked with the chalk tower. Behind it is the drop, and among the payment slips lies a page, damp but readable.
You know Elena's missing page is somewhere in the drop, so you go straight to it.

deductions.name: Where
deductions.finding: The light shows only on fog nights, and where no lighthouse stands. So it is no lighthouse. It is a ship that hides in the fog bank west of the Teeth and flashes the harbor alarm.
deductions.opens_line: Your crew can now call nightfall and hunt the light.

deductions.name: The seal
deductions.finding: The crates from the wrecks carry the seal that is on every keeper's key: the seal of the Harbor Office. The smugglers only carry the crates, for pay.
deductions.clear_line: This clears the fisherman: he is a smuggler, but not the one with the light.
deductions.opens_line: Follow the money: Greyfathom's manifest and the Harbor Office post can now be found.

deductions.name: The money
deductions.finding: Greyfathom holds twelve stolen lighthouse lenses for its owner, and the owner's post, a slip for every wreck, goes to the Harbor Office. The wrecks pay someone in the office, not the yard. Both papers carry the same chalk tower, and only one tower on this coast has no keeper: the old watchtower on the Teeth.
deductions.clear_line: This clears the salvage foreman: the foreman only runs the yard.
deductions.opens_line: The watchtower ruin on the Teeth can now be searched.
deductions.opens_line_with_lens: The watchtower ruin on the Teeth can now be searched, and relit with a lens.

deductions.name: The signal
deductions.finding: On every wreck night, Harbor Office orders sent the coastguard away. And the lit window across the bay is a decoy: whoever it belongs to is out at sea after dark.
deductions.clear_line: This clears the coastguard commander: the commander only followed orders.
deductions.opens_line: With D2, D3 and D4 on the board, your crew can make an accusation once the schooner is found.

muster.case_needs: a level 1 signal station on a player's home islet. Every player has a home islet, a True Keeper too, so every crew can build one.
muster.optional_extra: a level 1 workshop on plot_2, which makes a lens for the old watchtower (the ruin_light, tier should)
muster.reminder_line: Your crew will need a third light for the night. Build a signal station on your home islet.
muster.note: The muster only reminds. The crew can build later, during the case. Prices come from the open world: level 1 costs 300 coins and 10 timber, and every new player gets 20 timber once.

night.aimed_by: player, also for a light that a partner holds

aiming.where: In the browser. Aiming costs no request: the browser keeps each beam's bearing, and Lock sends it (POST /api/finale/signal {light, bearing, actionUid}).
aiming.beam_stays_aimed: A beam stays where it was aimed after its lock ends or is refused. Pressing Lock again re-sends that bearing.
aiming.aim_first_lock_later: One player may aim every beam first and then lock them one after another. All three locks must fall inside lock_seconds.
aiming.reserved_light_shows_its_beam: A light reserved by a partner order shows its beam at once, so a player can aim it while the partner sails. A lock is accepted only when the seat is on post: the partner has arrived, or the player has climbed.

night.locks_must_overlap: The fog parts when three accepted locks from three different seats at three different lights are all still held. So the last of the three must be accepted less than lock_seconds after the first.
night.bearing_rule: Compass degrees: 0 is north, 90 is east. bearing = atan2(dx, dy) in degrees, then modulo 360, where dx = schooner x minus light x (east is positive) and dy = light y minus schooner y (north is positive, because chart y grows to the south).

chart.axes: x grows to the east and y grows to the south, like the pixels of the sea chart (448 by 256 native pixels, D005). North is up.
chart.note: Light positions are copied from the place registry (frontend/src/world/places/registry.js): the place's chart position plus half the light's beamOrigin, with y flipped. A test keeps them equal (docs/story/CASE-FILE.md, section 17). The fog bank lies west of the Teeth marker (365, 65), where the registry puts the ruin. The G4 cinematic three_lights takes the schooner position as its target, because its default target is the Teeth marker, from where the two public lights are only 11 degrees apart.

lights.name: the Keeper's lamp
lights.note: The lamp has a zone of its own in the registry (the lamp room above the tower door). Every seat carries the brass key for the door. A True Keeper starts here.

lights.name: the Harbor Light
lights.note: A public light in the shared harbor.

lights.name: a home signal station
lights.note: Every player has a home islet, a True Keeper too, so every crew can build this light. All home islets share one chart position, so a crew counts one station, whoever built it. Any player of the crew may man it.

lights.name: the old watchtower
lights.note: An extra fourth light for later, not needed by any crew. A player makes one lens at a level 1 workshop on plot_2. A lens can be made at any time, also before D3 (decided 5 Nov 2026); only fitting it in the ruin waits for D3. Then any player of the crew may man it. The timing program does not need it because every crew can build a signal station.

lines.not_yet: Nobody knows what to hunt for yet. Solve D1 first.
lines.nightfall: Night falls on your crew's chart. Fog rolls in from the west, and far out past the Teeth a light starts to flash: long, short, long.
lines.on_post: You light {light} and swing its beam out over the fog.
lines.not_manned: Nobody is at that light yet.
lines.locked: Beam locked on the flashing light. It holds for 90 seconds.
lines.parted: Three beams cross in the fog. Where they meet, the fog thins, and a dark schooner rides at anchor with its lamp shuttered.
lines.dawn: Dawn breaks, and the fog keeps its secret. Your crew can call nightfall again in 3 minutes.

lines.aboard: You climb aboard. The masked captain stands at the wheel and says nothing.
lines.needs_schooner: There is nobody to accuse yet. Find the light first.
lines.needs_deductions: You need D2, D3 and D4 on your board before the charge will stick.
lines.wait: Your crew can accuse again in one minute.

lines.text: You pull back the captain's hood. It is the harbor master. He does not look surprised. 'Someone flashes the alarm,' he says, 'and I answer. I always have.'
Plot twist: the man who answered your alarm was the one sending it.
He posted a reward for finding a light he lit himself.
His office seal was on every crate, and every wreck paid into his post room.
On every wreck night, his orders sent the coastguard away.
His lit window was a lamp his night clerk kept burning while he sailed.

true_keeper.text: You flashed his own alarm with the whole bay watching, so he had to answer it. When your note came, his clerk blinked the window and the red boat ran. He let the coastguard take the fisherman, and his office freed him by morning. This time the light really is yours.

witness.text: Your note is how the red boat knew to run: his clerk blinked the window when it came. The harbor master never came, because he was already out at sea.

informant.text: 'Thanks for telling me where to look,' the fisherman said. He only ever carried the crates. The seal on every one of them was the harbor master's.

stranger.text: 'Whoever you are, nobody knows you're up there,' he called through the door. That is also why the yard would hire you. Every lens on its manifest was bought with a wreck and held for the harbor master.

log_reader_line.text: Elena wrote 'Tell the harbor master.' before she knew. The page that was torn out said the rest.

last_beat.text: His ledger counts the stolen lenses waiting at Gull's Rest: eleven. Greyfathom's manifest said twelve. One lens is missing.

rewards.contributor: A player seat with at least one accepted pin, one of the three locks that parted the fog, or the accepted accusation. Partners never earn.
rewards.partner_pin_counts_for: the player who gave the pin order (ordered_by in NPC-PARTNERS.md)
rewards.part_of_a_deduction: You pinned one of its two cards, or ordered a partner's pin of it, before the deduction formed.
rewards.finale_role: You made one of the three locks that parted the fog (a lock you aimed for a partner's light counts), or you made the accepted accusation.

coins.when: your first accepted pin of each card, in any crew
a deduction forms and you are part of it
the accusation is accepted, to every contributor

paid_routes.partner_ref: false_light:{crew_id}:npc:{order_uid}, as NPC-PARTNERS.md rule N17 says. At most 12 + 36 + 5 + 64 = 117 characters, under the wallet limit of 120.
paid_routes.note: A paid route is refused, and nothing is charged, when that seat already holds the card.

keepsakes.text: The title Relighter, next to your captain name.
A Keeper's Star over your home on every chart.
Your captain name on the Wall of Lights in Saltreach Harbor.
A recovered lens for your signal station. It cannot be traded.
One line in your journal, from your kit and whether you read the log.

epilogue_lines.true_keeper: Flashed the alarm, kept the light, and found out who was answering it.
epilogue_lines.witness: Sent a warning to the wrong man, then proved it.
epilogue_lines.informant: Trusted the fisherman, then followed his crates to the seal.
epilogue_lines.stranger: Took no side, and saw what both sides were hiding.

relighting.trigger: the first accepted accusation by any crew in the live world

world_stage.how: one conditional database update, so it happens exactly once, and only while the relight lock is open

relighting.relight_lock: One server setting keeps the relight switch locked until the game opens. While it is locked, an accepted accusation still pays its rewards and plays the reveal, but the world stays dark. So the test solves of the team cannot relight the live coast.
relighting.rehearsals: There is no separate demo world for now. Rehearsals and the class demo use the ?demo=1 highlights tour, which runs in the browser on a stand-in and never touches the live world.

for_everyone.text: Every public lighthouse on the shared chart comes on, and the night lanes are lit.
The fog bank west of the Teeth rolls back. The false light no longer shows on real fog nights.
Gull's Rest opens: a new place behind the old fog line, where the stolen lenses are kept.

Greyfathom Salvage leaves the Island Exchange and every holder is cashed out at the last price. This needs a change to D017, which has no delisting yet (OPEN-WORLD.md, section 7.7). Until then the company stays listed and nothing else in this list depends on it.
Fees drop: Exchange fees from 2% to 1% each way. This needs L4 to read the world stage, because the built Exchange has a fixed 2%. Fast travel has no fee for now, so there is nothing to lower there.
The Relighting Festival: 48 hours of double salvage on every driftline, fireworks at night and a free lantern colour.
The Wall of Lights goes up in Saltreach Harbor with the first crew's captain names.

later_crews.text: Each later crew adds its captain names to the Wall of Lights and lights one more lamp on the shared chart.

spoiler_rule.rule: Anything that names or shows the culprit appears only to players who have solved the case, in any crew.
covers: the reveal, the closing lines and the epilogue lines
the jailed harbor master and his lines
the Lightkeepers' Hall in the old Harbor Office
the ledger and the papers at Gull's Rest
the reason Greyfathom left the Exchange
spoiler_rule.everyone_else_sees: The false light is out. A crew found it.
spoiler_rule.wall_shows: captain names and the order of solving, nothing else
spoiler_rule.inside_a_case: Inside an unsolved case every place shows its case state, even to a player who solved the case in another crew.

crews_still_on_the_case: They see the relit chart, Gull's Rest, the lower fees and the Wall of Lights (names only), like everyone.

Their case keeps working: the Harbor Office with its notice board, counter, back room and lit window, Greyfathom's yard, the cove, the jail's release order and the ruin stay as they were, in their case view.
On their own case nights, their fog bank and false light are drawn for their crew only.
If Greyfathom is delisted, the share route to C6 closes. The True Keeper's back room, the paid clerk and the mail boat stay open.

partners.rules: docs/story/NPC-PARTNERS.md owns partner orders, errand minutes, the kit order and partner titles.
partners.lines: backend/content/partners.json holds every word a partner says, including one found line and one pinned line per card.
partners.kit_order_note: Decided 5 Nov 2026. An empty seat takes the first kit in this list that no player holds. NPC-PARTNERS.md section 4.2 has the rule, and the timing program keeps the same order.
partners.takeover_kit: A friend who takes over a partner's seat keeps their own kit (decided 5 Nov 2026). The seat number, the satchel and the pins stay.
partners.paid_note: A partner uses a paid route only when the order says allowPaid (NPC-PARTNERS.md, section 5.4). Without it, paid routes do not exist for the partner. Decided 5 Nov 2026: allowPaid is off unless the player allows it for that order, and the team confirms this at kickoff because it touches coins. The 23 Nov minimum leaves allowPaid off.
partners.paid_route_charged_to: the player who gave the order

planning.note: Planning numbers, not rules. The simulated run is docs/story/TIMING.md, and a human paper playtest is still owed. A crossing takes about 4 to 6 seconds, up to 15 in fog or storm (OPEN-WORLD.md 5.2), so most of a route's minutes are finding the spot, the timer and reading.
planning.estimate_formula: estimate_minutes = crossing + finding the spot + timer_minutes + reading, for a player who sets off from Saltreach Harbor. Waiting for a window comes on top.
